sections.content:
Malaysia's DE Rantau Nomad Pass is the country's dedicated visa for remote workers and digital nomads. Tech professionals need to demonstrate annual income of at least 24,000 US dollars, roughly 2,000 dollars per month, while non-tech professionals must show 60,000 dollars per year. Bank statements or client contracts serve as proof.

Beyond income, applicants need at least 3 years of professional experience, valid health insurance covering their stay, and a clean criminal record. Applications are submitted online through MDEC, the Malaysia Digital Economy Corporation, which administers the program.

The pass is issued for 3 to 12 months and can be renewed, allowing total stays of up to 24 months. The fee is 1,000 Malaysian ringgit, about 220 US dollars, for the main applicant and 500 ringgit per dependent. Processing typically takes 2 to 6 weeks from submission.

One key restriction: pass holders cannot work for Malaysian companies or serve Malaysian clients. All income must come from foreign employers or clients, keeping the program focused on importing foreign spending power rather than competing with local workers.

The pass covers Peninsular Malaysia, including popular nomad hubs like Kuala Lumpur, Penang, and Langkawi. Note that Sabah and Sarawak on Borneo are excluded from the program, so plan your travels accordingly. Your spouse and children can accompany you as dependents.

Malaysia's appeal for nomads is strong: fast internet, affordable high-quality living, excellent food, and a central Southeast Asian location. Combined with the straightforward MDEC application process, the DE Rantau Pass is one of the region's most accessible nomad visas.
